subject: Science
board: National Curriculum (EYFS: Understanding the World - The Natural World)
source: National Curriculum / EYFS Understanding the World; Drive Science folder 'Science lower school' topic folders (3.8 organisms, 3.7 earth) used as a guide to topics

lessons.unit: Understanding the World: Autumn and the natural world
lessons.title: Autumn leaves and trees
objectives: Say that autumn is a season and that leaves change colour
Sort leaves by colour and size
Use words such as red, brown, big and small to describe a leaf

keywords.def: the season when leaves change colour and fall off trees
the flat green part of a tree or plant
a very tall plant with a trunk and branches

starter: Let's say Bismillah together. Can you wave hello to our friends on the screen?
What colour is the sky today? What colour is grass?
Show me something you can see outside your window.

teach.heading: Look at a tree
teach.note: Show a clear photo or hold up a real branch. Ask children to point to the trunk, branches and leaves on their own screen, then in their garden or window. Praise every answer.

teach.heading: It is autumn
bullets: Leaves turn red, orange and brown
teach.note: Show photos of a green leaf and an autumn leaf. Ask 'What is different?' Children may say 'it is dead'; gently say the tree is getting ready for winter. Say 'autumn' together three times.

teach.heading: Colours and sizes
bullets: Some leaves are red or yellow
teach.note: Hold up two leaves (real ones, or pictures). Ask 'Which one is bigger?' Model the sentence 'This leaf is big and brown.' Children repeat it.

teach.heading: Allah made trees
bullets: Trees are a gift from Allah
teach.note: Link to gratitude in simple words. Ask 'What do trees give us?' (shade, fruit, a place for birds). Keep it joyful. We never pick leaves off living trees; only use leaves that have already fallen.

practice: Hold up a leaf. Tell me: is it big or small?
Point to the red leaf, then the brown leaf, in the pictures I show you.
Say the sentence with me: 'The leaf is yellow.'
independent: Draw an autumn tree with a trunk, branches and falling leaves. Use red, orange and brown crayons.
Sort three leaves (or three coloured paper squares) into big and small.
exit: Which season has leaves falling down: autumn or summer?
What colour can an autumn leaf be? Say two colours.
lessons.homework: With a grown-up, look at a tree and tell them one colour you can see on its leaves.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use real objects and point-and-name; accept pointing or one-word answers. Stretch: ask children to describe a leaf using two describing words.

lessons.unit: Understanding the World: Autumn and the natural world
lessons.title: My five senses
objectives: Match each sense to a body part
Describe something using a sense word

keywords.def: the ways we find out about the world: see, hear, smell, taste, touch
the parts of our body we use to see
the parts of our body we use to hear

starter: Bismillah. Can you show me a smile and wave? Which part of your body did you use to wave?
Can you point to your nose, your ears and your eyes?
What colour is a leaf in autumn?

teach.heading: Seeing and hearing
bullets: Eyes and ears help us learn
teach.note: Children point to eyes then ears. Play a short sound (clap, bell) with the microphone on. Ask 'What did you hear?' Praise careful listening.

teach.heading: Smelling and tasting
teach.note: Safe online activity: a grown-up at home may offer a piece of orange or a spoon of honey if the child has no allergies; otherwise talk about foods using pictures. Never ask children to taste unknown items.

teach.heading: Touching
teach.note: Ask children to find something soft (a cushion) and something hard (a toy) at home and bring it to the screen. Model the words soft, hard, rough, smooth.

teach.heading: Thank you Allah
teach.note: Simple gratitude. Mention that Allah gave us hearing and sight (Qur'an 16:78) in child-friendly words only: 'Allah gave us ears and eyes.' Keep it short and warm.

practice: Touch your nose. Which sense do we use it for: smelling or hearing?
I will ring a bell. Close your eyes. Which sense are you using?
Find something soft at home and show it to the screen.
independent: Draw a face with big eyes, ears, a nose and a mouth.
Draw one thing you like to smell and one thing you like to hear.
exit: What do we use our ears for?
Which part of your body do you see with?
lessons.homework: Tell a grown-up about your five senses. Point to each body part as you say it.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use gestures and real objects; allow pointing. Stretch: children say a full sentence such as 'I smell with my nose.'

lessons.unit: Understanding the World: Autumn and the natural world
lessons.title: Animals and what they eat
objectives: Say that animals need food and water
Match an animal to the food it eats

keywords.def: a living thing that moves and needs food and water
an animal that people look after at home
what animals and people eat to stay alive and grow

starter: Bismillah. Make the sound of a cat. Make the sound of a cow.
Which part of your body do you use to see?
What season has red and brown leaves?

teach.heading: Animals all around
bullets: Cows and sheep live on farms
teach.note: Show pictures one by one. Children name each animal and make its sound. Use the animals' names in English and encourage home-language names too.

teach.heading: Animals need food
teach.note: Ask 'What do you eat? What do you drink?' Link to the child's own needs. Say 'animals are alive, like us'.

teach.heading: Who eats what?
teach.note: Match pictures of animals to food with a pointing game. Misconception: all animals eat the same food. Ask 'Would a rabbit eat fish?' and laugh together.

teach.heading: Being kind to animals
bullets: We give pets food and water
teach.note: Teach gentleness and kindness to animals as part of Islamic adab. Ask 'How can we be kind to a cat?' (give water, be gentle, do not shout).

practice: Point to the animal that says 'moo'.
What does a rabbit like to eat? Choose a carrot or a fish.
independent: Draw your favourite animal and the food it eats.
Draw a bowl of water for a pet.
exit: Name one animal that lives on a farm.
What do all animals need to stay alive: food or toys?
lessons.homework: Look for an animal or a bird near your home or on a picture. Tell a grown-up its name and what it eats.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use real toy animals and sounds; accept one-word answers. Stretch: children say what an animal eats and what it drinks.

lessons.unit: Understanding the World: Autumn and the natural world
lessons.title: Autumn weather
objectives: Name types of weather: sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy
Choose clothes that suit the weather
Say what the weather is today

keywords.def: what it is like outside: sunny, rainy, windy or cloudy
moving air that we can feel

starter: Bismillah. Look out of your window. Is it light or dark?
Name two parts of a tree.
Name one animal and say what it eats.

teach.heading: What is the weather?
bullets: Weather is what it is like outside
teach.note: Show four weather pictures. Children copy actions: arms in a circle for sun, fingers wiggling for rain, blowing for wind. Look outside and decide today's weather together.

teach.heading: Autumn is windy and rainy
teach.note: Safe demo: drop a real leaf or a small piece of paper and blow it to show wind. Ask 'What moved the leaf?'

teach.heading: Clothes for the weather
bullets: Wear a coat when it is cold
Wear wellies when it is rainy
Wear a hat in the sun
teach.note: Hold up or show pictures of clothes. Children choose for each weather. Talk about being safe and warm.

teach.heading: Rain is a gift
teach.note: Link to gratitude. Simple message: rain helps plants grow and gives animals and people water. Connect to Qur'an 6:99 only in the simplest way: 'Allah sends down rain and plants grow.'

practice: Show me with your hands what rain looks like.
It is rainy. Which do you choose: a coat or sunglasses?
Tell me the weather today: 'Today it is ...'
independent: Draw a picture of rainy weather with a puddle and clouds.
Draw yourself in your autumn clothes.
exit: What is falling from the cloud when it is rainy?
What do we wear on our feet when it is rainy?
lessons.homework: Look outside each day this week and tell a grown-up what the weather is.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use actions and pictures for each weather word. Stretch: children say a sentence with 'because', such as 'I wear a coat because it is cold.'
